newsitem.title: USA: Transocean sees Q4 trailing expectations.
newsitem.headline: Transocean sees Q4 trailing expectations.

text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc said Monday preliminary fourth quarter operating results were below the current average earnings expectation of industry analysts.

It said indications are that earnings per share in the latest quarter were about $0.15 to $0.20 below the $0.55 which is the current average expectation of industry analysts. In the fourth quarter of 1995, the company earned $0.39.
It said the earnings shortfall is primarily due to higher operating expenses on certain rigs within its mobile rig fleet and unsatisfactory performance from its U.S. Gulf of Mexico turnkey operation.

The elevated operating expenses within the mobile rig fleet are chiefly due to higher than anticipated levels of repair and replacement activity on certain North Sea rigs and high non-recurring startup costs on two of the company's jackup rigs, the Interocean III and Offshore Jupiter, Transocean said.
The additional repair and replacement costs incurred on the North Sea rigs approximate $3.0 to $4.0 million.
The Interocean III and Offshore Jupiter were in shipyards for much of the period while undergoing preparations for new contracts.
The high startup costs experienced on these two rigs resulted in a combined estimated operating loss of $3.6 million during the period, Transocean said.
It said the Interocean III left the shipyard on November 25 and started a new contract on December 19 with Enron Corp in India which is estimated to run until late 1997.

The Offshore Jupiter, after being stacked for over three years, left the shipyard and commenced a new contract on December 1 with Bunduq in the Arab Gulf. This contract is estimated to run through April 1997.
Unsatisfactory performance in the company's U.S. Gulf of Mexico turnkey operation has resulted in a preliminary estimated operating loss of $4.7 million for the period.

Losses were recorded on four wells due to operational difficulties which delayed completion of each project, the company said. Two of these wells remain in progress and are expected to be completed in February 1997.
Transocean has initiated changes in its U.S. Gulf of Mexico turnkey organization which should improve future performance, the company's statement said without providing any details.
Final results for the three and twelve months ended December 31 will be announced on February 18, it said.
